title.narrative: Integrated Health Response to Malnutrition and Gender-Based Violence in Haiti's Crisis Context

description.narrative: Malnutrition remains one of the most pressing public health challenges in Haiti, deeply intertwined with the country's ongoing crises of insecurity, widespread poverty, and limited access to essential healthcare services. Children are disproportionately affected, especially those living in internally displaced persons (IDP) sites, where conditions are dire, and the risk of life-threatening complications from severe malnutrition is alarmingly high. Despite various interventions, persistent gaps in early detection, robust referral systems, and adequate treatment capacities continue to endanger child survival. Simultaneously, Haiti is navigating a multifaceted humanitarian crisis, marked by an escalating wave of violence. Women and girls are particularly vulnerable, as gender-based violence (GBV), including sexual violence and rape, has increasingly become a tool of terror, often deployed as a weapon of war in the most conflict-ridden areas. This dual burden of malnutrition and GBV has created an urgent need for integrated, comprehensive responses to address these overlapping emergencies.This project seeks to tackle these critical challenges by focusing on two core objectives: improving the detection, referral, and treatment of severe malnutrition cases with complications, and enhancing the medical and psychosocial response to GBV. The intervention on malnutrition emphasizes strengthening local capacities and promoting life-saving practices like exclusive breastfeeding. In partnership with the Direction Sanitaire de l’Ouest (DSO), healthcare workers and community agents will be mobilized across 54 IDP sites to identify and refer malnourished children with complications to appropriate care. Concurrently, targeted support will be provided to breastfeeding mothers in these communities. Three hospitals will be equipped and their staff trained to implement the "10 Steps of Successful Breastfeeding," while seven stabilization units and related health institutions in the metropolitan area will be enhanced to deliver high-quality care to children with severe malnutrition. In order to address this challenge, this proposal was developed in collaboration with UNICEF to ensure that there are no duplications and to promote complementarity in our efforts. One of the key areas of synergy is that PAHO/WHO will focus specifically targeting children suffering from severe malnutrition with complications, as per its mandate, while UNICEF will address other forms of malnutrition. To address the GBV crisis, the project will strengthen the health system's capacity to provide comprehensive care for survivors, including critical mental health services. Interventions will support nine selected health facilities in the metropolitan area to establish high-quality services tailored to the needs of GBV survivors, particularly those referred from IDP sites. The one-stop GBV response center will be reactivated to offer holistic medical and psychosocial care, while health workers and community organizations will receive training to better address GBV and mental health issues. The GBV hotline and mental health helplines will also be reactivated, ensuring that survivors have access to timely support. Additional efforts will focus on improving access to GBV and mental health services within 30 IDP sites and conducting awareness campaigns, monitoring, and supervision activities to sustain the project's impact.By combining targeted efforts to combat malnutrition with a robust response to GBV, this project aims not only to address the immediate health and safety needs of Haiti's most vulnerable populations but also to build resilience and strengthen the foundation for long-term recovery and development.
